''''' Phygelius aequalis''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Scrophulariaceae, [[native plant|native]] to South Africa. It is a semi-[[evergreen]] [[shrub]] growing to {{convert|1|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} tall and wide, with {{convert|25|cm|0|abbr=on}} long panicles of pink flowers with crimson lobes and yellow throats.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|page=1136}}</ref> This species may be distinguished from the closely related ''[[Phygelius capensis]]'' by the fact that the flowers grow in a single plane along one side of the stem. The narrowly tubular flowers are up to {{convert|6|cm|0|abbr=on}} in length.

The common names '''Cape fuchsia''' and '''Cape figwort''' attach to both ''P. aequalis'' and ''P. capensis'', though they are not closely related to the true [[fuchsia]]s, and "figwort" refers to several plants other than phygelius.

''Phygelius aequalis'' is valued as a garden plant with a particularly long flowering season throughout summer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.plantzafrica.com/plantnop/phygelaequal.htm|title=Phygelius aequalis {{!}} PlantZAfrica.com|website=www.plantzafrica.com|access-date=2018-10-18}}</ref> Though a shrub, in cooler areas it grows as a [[perennial plant|perennial]]. It requires some winter protection. The [[cultivars]] 'Trewidden Pink' <ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/176155/Phygelius-aequalis-Trewidden-Pink/Details | title = ''Phygelius aequalis'' 'Trewidden Pink' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 18 January 2021}}</ref> and 'Yellow Trumpet' <ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/97696/Phygelius-aequalis-Yellow-Trumpet/Details | title = ''Phygelius aequalis'' 'Yellow Trumpet' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 18 January 2021}}</ref> have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 78 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society 
| access-date = 25 April 2018}}</ref>
